text: I am Dr. Agent. speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, and a history of tics treated with haloperidol is highly suggestive of NMS, a medical emergency often misdiagnosed as meningoencephalitis due to the absence of headache or nuchal rigidity. I request immediate serum creatine kinase (CK) and electrolyte levels to confirm muscle breakdown and rule out other causes.
